correctness.rationale: Faces through 0 give coordinate deletion and strictly positive retained barycentric weights, including the positive remaining weight at 0. For a face indexed by I not containing 0, the foot has retained coordinates b_i+λ_I/L_i, with λ_I>0 by the strict interior hypothesis. The origin normal cell is exactly the box [0,b_1]×…×[0,b_d]. At v_i set t=L_i(x_i−b_i); then the normal constraints are t≥0 and x_j≤b_j+t/L_j for j≠i. The original simplex constraints reduce to 0≤x_j for j≠i and the slanted top. In the full-dimensional cell, bottom t=0 and top cannot meet because at t=0 all x_j≤b_j and Σ b_j/L_j<1. Each upper/lower coordinate pair is also disjoint. A vertex needs d independent active inequalities, hence one per pair; all 2^d choices solve uniquely and feasibly as exactly the two families of feet, with independent active normals. Thus all stated inequalities really are facets and compatible intersections are precisely partial choices of the pairs, giving the cube and the antipodal v_i (top and lower choices) and B (bottom and upper choices). South/north intersections work coordinatewise in the cube, giving O1–O2. O3 can be checked directly: the edge at v_i for the bottom/top swap is along e_i, normal to the north facet t=0. The edge at v_i for a j-swap is along v_j−v_i, normal to the north facet x_j=b_j+t/L_j. At 0 it is coordinate perpendicularity. The inspected conditional Proposition 4.2 can also be used once the combinatorics and distinct projection vertices have established admissibility. Every point has at least one support-score maximizing vertex and two distinct cells meet on their tie hyperplane, a face of both. This verifies the normal-cell equality and face-to-face tiling for all allowed B and leg lengths, not just symmetric anchors or lengths.
residual_risks: The cubes are combinatorial and need not be orthogonal boxes. Finite checks cannot settle the full-dimensional range; the proof here uses the right-simplex geometry explicitly.

evidence: Theorem 6.6 gives the equivalence in dimension three and Remark 6.9 records the low-dimensional implication. The higher-dimensional general implication is Conjecture 6.8. Proposition 4.2 requires admissibility, and Lemma 6.3 requires the geometric cutout condition as well as the kernel.

Companion Proposition 5.15 provides an all-dimensional apex result for a cone section satisfying the relative-interior fan incidence condition (I), with axial anchor and its specified pyramid construction. Proposition 5.16 also characterizes such bipolar realizations; neither asserts that all perpendicular sections of the arbitrary anchored right simplices satisfy (I). Lemma 5.12 gives only one direction of (I) under reciprocity.
The same-day orthogonal product result extends low-dimensional factors, not a single indecomposable higher-dimensional right simplex.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The apex result genuinely overlaps with the local geometry after conditions are proved. Re-expressing a tangent cone as an axial pyramid does not verify the interval condition or show its normal restriction is untruncated by the actual opposite simplex facet. The inspected sufficient conditions do not directly supply this uniform right-simplex assertion.

originality.rationale: The distinct conclusion supported by the inspected literature is the uniform metric result for right simplices, at every interior anchor and at every vertex, including dimensions at least four. The prior cube combinatorics, always-existing normal-fan tiling, conditional apex cutout machinery and low-dimensional results are substantial overlaps and are not claimed as new. The inspection does not establish historical priority for the remaining metric result.
residual_risks: Historical work on classical or metric cubical subdivisions could establish earlier right-simplex coverage; the targeted literature comparison is not exhaustive. The conditional apex mechanism and abstract cubical subdivision are known and must not be credited as new.
